study type: Longitudinal cohort study with repeated measures design
outcome: Body composition (total fat mass %, lean mass %, skeletal muscle mass %, trunk lean mass %)
cohort: 634 offsprings (aged 10 to 21 years, 52% female) from the Early Life Exposure in Mexico to Environmental Toxicants birth cohort.
finding: Despite sex-specific associations of breastfeeding duration with body composition (e.g., lower fat mass and higher lean mass in boys with 5 months breastfeeding; positive trend for trunk lean mass in girls), there was a lack of substantial evidence for protective effects of breastfeeding against impaired cardiometabolic health during adolescence.
